patients.label: 50-year-old dark-skinned woman with Addison’s disease, Graves’ disease with hyperthyroidism and multifocal oral melanoacanthoma
attribution_limitations: Slight itching accompanied the growth reported at anamnesis, while the examination paragraph calls the lesions asymptomatic; the statements concern different time frames and are not a numeric source conflict. Both are kept; no resolution is inferred.

The patient is described as being treated and monitored for both Graves’ disease and Addison’s disease, yet no medication for Addison’s disease had been initiated; not a value conflict (monitoring without medication is possible). No treatment for Addison’s disease is inferred.

"The adrenal insufficiency" probably refers back to the reported Addison’s disease, but the source does not state the identity; kept as two literal condition statements and not merged. The adrenal diagnosis is dated only as the same period that the pigmented lesions appeared, whose own onset time is not stated.

The parenthesis "(TSH 1.33 mU/L, FT4 0.87 ng/dL, cortisol 13.59 µg/dL)" follows the statement that the cortisol levels were within the normal range; only cortisol is flagged normal. Its sentence states no time, and the preceding sentence names follow-up assessments, not these tests, so no time is assigned. Two FT4 values are printed, the "current" 2.04 ng/dL in the anamnesis and 0.87 ng/dL in the follow-up paragraph; the source does not make them the same measurement or time point, so they are two observations, not a source conflict. Neither is flagged high or low.

The 2014 Graves’ disease diagnosis was "based on" thyroid scintigraphy and blood tests (TSH 0.01 mU/L, TRAB 2.68 IU/L); the test dates are not stated (no time assigned to the tests) and the scintigraphy result is not described.

Discussion: lesions "requiring no treatment, as in the patient described in this report". Whether the clause covers only "requiring no treatment" or the other listed lesion attributes is not literal; no treatment item is recorded for the melanoacanthoma and nothing is copied from the general description.
